column1: # Every committed boundary artifact, bound to its content hash AND its closure hash.
# THE LAW (`CLAUDE.md` section 0, lesson 1): *"Bind every deposit to its content hash AND its
# closure hash, with a verifier."* The verifier is `tools/boundary_artifacts.py`; it exits non-zero
# and names what disagreed. Re-seed with `--write` only after a DELIBERATE rebuild, and say so.
# A boundary artifact is a compiled binary committed into the tree because the host workspace
# carries the artifact without carrying the toolchain that made it. Nothing in `cargo test`
# recompiles one, so source and artifact drift SILENTLY. That is not hypothetical:
#   `soma/kernel/soma.spv` at sha256 9a805973… was NOT produced by this repository at any commit.
#   It is byte-identical to `a07ff376:src/soma/kernel/soma.spv` in the frozen laboratory, whose last
#   commit touching that path is e714ebc0, 2026-07-14. `FeltLineage::required_carrier_depth` — the
#   continuation-depth carrier mechanism the current `carriage.rs` compiles — does not exist at
#   e714ebc0; it entered at 323522b7, 2026-07-20, six days LATER. The committed artifact therefore
#   predated the law it was supposed to be an image of, in a tree where nothing could notice.
# `rebuild_evidence` is PROVENANCE, not a check. It records whether anyone has actually reproduced
# the committed bytes from the declared closure. `CLAUDE.md` section 8: grade the implementation,
# not the receipt — so an artifact that has never been reproduced says so in the registry rather
# than borrowing the authority of the two hashes beside it.
# Columns: record, artifact, key, value. `consumer` may repeat. `entry` is required by
# PATH_INCLUDES only. CLOSURE rows carry one source file and its sha256 each; `closure_sha256` is
# the sha256 over the path-ordered `path<TAB>sha256` table of all of them.
